articles.title: Aoandon: Hearn's ghost stories in Japanese, retold at five JLPT levels
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine In Edo Japan, friends sometimes spent a night telling a hundred ghost stories. It was called hyakumonog…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine In Edo Japan, friends sometimes spent a night telling a hundred ghost stories. It was called hyakumonogatari. A hundred wicks burned inside a lantern covered with blue paper, in a room away from the guests. After each story, the teller walked to that room and put out one flame. The legend says that when the last flame goes out, the spirit of the blue lantern appears. Her name is Aoandon, 青行灯. The Japanese ghost stories most people outside Japan know come from Lafcadio Hearn. Hearn never properly learned Japanese. His wife, Koizumi Setsu, found the old stories and told them to him in her own words, and his book Kwaidan grew out of those tellings.
articles.author: ADK BBX

articles.body: Free kit: animated pieces + 8 AI prompts → https://qodesign.dev/free?utm_source=devto&utm_medium=tutorial&utm_campaign=tutorial8&utm_content=top Every dashboard you generate with Cursor, v0 or Lovable has a delete button somewhere. Usually it's a red button that opens an "Are you sure?" modal, and after the third time people click "Yes" without reading it. A hold-to-delete button fixes that with less UI. You press and hold, a fill sweeps across, and the delete only happens if you keep holding to the end. Let go early and it drains back. Nobody deletes a file by accident, and there's no modal. This week I went through the most-favorited buttons on uiverse.io. The top ones all do the same kind of thing: a round icon button stretches into a pill and something new appears.

articles.title: I Taught Open-Source AI to Listen to the Ghosts of Broken Machines
articles.excerpt: This is our team submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. A machine stops talking when its experiment ends. Its sensors do not. Somewhere in the UCI hy…
articles.body: This is our team submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built A machine stops talking when its experiment ends. Its sensors do not. Somewhere in the UCI hydraulic systems archive , experiment 735 left behind sixty seconds of pressure, flow, temperature, vibration, and power measurements. The pressure rises, levels off, falls, and rises again. The recording has a known experimental condition—but what happens if an AI model tells a different story? That question became ECHO-17: The Machine That Remembers , an interactive, open-AI-powered forensic lab for real historical machine recordings.

articles.title: What it actually costs to build an app, and how to compare two quotes
articles.excerpt: Nobody can price an app from one sentence. Here is what the price is actually made of, and how to get a quote you can compare against another one. Short answer: The number comes from screens, sign-in,…
articles.body: Nobody can price an app from one sentence. Here is what the price is actually made of, and how to get a quote you can compare against another one. Short answer: The number comes from screens, sign-in, payments, admin screens and integrations, not from the idea. Small jobs start at $50. A full product is quoted as one fixed price after a free call. Store accounts, hosting and any AI bill are running costs, separate from the build. The cheapest quote usually leaves something out that you pay to add back later. Why do two developers quote different numbers? Because they are not quoting the same thing. One is quoting the app you described, and the other is quoting the app you will want in six months: the admin screen, the refunds, the offline mode, the second language.

articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. articles.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

articles.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
articles.excerpt: In space, no one can hear you scream, a bit like the empty theater screens that some horror franchise's final installments limp. But there are still some real gems among the space-based frightfests.
articles.body: In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1.
